## What’s new
- Notes on invoices, payables, and companies: each note shows who added it and when, newest first. Notes are searchable, and you can choose who gets an email about a new note. - Names of other records are now links. Clients, people, projects, invoices, and payables mentioned on a record open that record, including invoice line items, related payables, a payable’s “What for,” and matches in Banking. - A brief network interruption no longer signs Beacon out.

## What’s new
- Days your other Mac sent before 1.0.57 with an “Arc history” problem can now be analyzed. Browser history never blocks a review. - A Mac now re-sends a day that had a capture problem once the problem is fixed.

## What’s new
- A Mac that doesn’t use Arc no longer stops your other Mac from analyzing a day. - Beacon now reads Vivaldi and Safari history, as well as Arc, to fill gaps in your browsing time. Visits synced from your iPhone count too. - A browser history problem shows as a warning on the day instead of blocking the review.

## What’s new
- Editing a recommended time log syncs to your other Macs, so everyone sees the edited version. If it’s edited in two places, the newer edit wins. - Merging recommendations works across your Macs too. - Approving a recommendation after moving it to a different project now keeps the new project.

## What’s new
- Recommended time logs are shared between your Macs. The Mac that prepares them uploads each day, and every Mac signed in as you shows the same recommendations in Day and Week view. - Approve, exclude, approve several at once, or undo from any Mac. A recommendation can only ever become one time log, even if you approve it on two Macs. - An approved log appears right away, and its billing details fill in on the next sync. - Recommendations you already approved or excluded on the reviewing Mac carry over.

## What’s new
- Daily review catches up on missed days. If the Mac that prepares your recommended time logs wasn’t open when a day came due, Beacon now goes back and prepares every day it missed in the last two weeks, newest first, instead of skipping them. - A day that can’t be prepared yet (for example, another Mac hasn’t shared that day’s activity) is retried later without holding up the other days. - Days with no activity are marked done quietly, without a notification.

## What’s new
- New time logs start with a single description bullet, ready to type. - Editing a log, adding one (⌘N), and dragging out a new log on the timeline now open in a panel on the right, so the calendar stays in view. In narrow windows the panel floats and the week scrolls sideways to show the days behind it. - One click opens a time log on the Day and Week timelines. Dragging a log or its resize handles never opens it. - Week view: click and drag across empty time to add a log, resize handles appear on hover, and each block shows the company’s emoji. The week now opens near your earliest work instead of at 12 AM. - Reviewing recommended logs in Week view: a tray along the bottom lists the selected day’s recommendations. Approve, edit, or exclude them while you look at the week, or tick several and approve them together with one undo. Days with recommendations waiting show a count badge. - Signing in on a new Mac now brings down all your clients, projects, and time-log history. - Client names, emoji, and colours, and project names, now sync between your Macs. The first time a Mac syncs, its own clients and projects are kept.

## What’s new
- Two-Mac daily review: simultaneous work for different clients or projects on different Macs is kept as separate parallel work. Only the same work seen from both Macs (for example, driving a Mac mini thread from T3 Code or Screen Sharing on the MacBook) is counted once.

## What’s new
- Two Macs, one daily review: Settings › Capture › This Mac now has a Role. Set a second Mac to Capture only and it keeps capturing, publishes its app activity, Codex/T3, and Arc evidence for that day, and never runs reviews or sends to client apps. Your Reviewer Mac includes that evidence, labelled with the Mac's name, in the daily review. - The daily review won't run on an incomplete day: if a Capture-only Mac hasn't published, a review is blocked with a clear message and an explicit "Analyze without" option. - Screen Sharing time that overlaps the other Mac's work is no longer counted twice.

## What’s new
- Companies › Connections: link a company to an existing QuickBooks customer or vendor. Search QuickBooks, pick the record, and change or unlink it later. Beacon only saves the link; QuickBooks isn't changed. - QuickBooks Bills for a payee paid through their company now use the payee's established QuickBooks vendor when the company has no vendor linked, instead of failing. - Sign in with Passwords: if no Beacon login is saved, the button now says so instead of doing nothing, and Beacon offers to save your login to Passwords after you sign in with your email and password. - Banking: match transactions to invoices and payables, pair transfers (including loan accounts), split transactions, record statement balances, categorize many at once, review suggestions, and import QuickBooks checking CSVs. - Payroll: fixed-salary setup with a quarterly Form 941 screen and filled IRS PDF.
